title: Productivity suite admin console: users, sign-in and audit settings
source_system: Productivity suite admin console (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Business plan with one user, the owner, as administrator; MFA is on with an authenticator app on the owner's phone, the only registered second factor; the provider keeps sign-in and sharing history; no saved review or export of that history

title: Productivity suite file storage: sync, retention and sharing report
source_system: Productivity suite admin console and sync client (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: The Customer Machine Library folder on the laptop syncs to cloud storage; deleted files and prior versions are kept 30 days; the activity history shows no restore; the sharing report lists 3 'anyone with the link' links to customer program folders, created in 2025 and 2026

title: Customer Machine Library folder review
source_system: Customer Machine Library folder (SYS-03 and SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About 2,400 files for about 70 machines at 10 customer sites: PLC logic, HMI projects, drive parameter files, CNC cutting programs and coil winding recipes, plus substation monitoring unit configuration and firmware files; each visit's files are saved with the visit date in the file name; no index of machines, no record of which version is current, and no hash values

title: Cloud storage file search: customer machine password spreadsheet
source_system: Productivity suite file storage (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: An ordinary spreadsheet, with no password or encryption on the file, lists about 140 customer machine passwords (PLC, HMI, drive and plant Wi-Fi) for 10 sites

title: Accounting SaaS users and security settings
source_system: Accounting SaaS settings (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: Business plan holding quotes, invoices, payments, the bank feed and customer remittance details; two named accounts: the owner's administrator account, which signs in with a password only although MFA is offered, and the bookkeeper's accountant-role login, which signs in through the CPA firm's account with MFA; the provider keeps sign-in history

title: Service laptop settings review
source_system: Service laptop settings screens (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: One local account with administrator rights, used for email, web, quotes and engineering work; built-in full-disk encryption on, with the recovery key stored offline; built-in antivirus on with real-time and scheduled scans; automatic OS updates on and update history current; host firewall on; engineering software from 5 automation makers installed; SaaS passwords saved in the browser; the IT consultant's remote-support tool installed with unattended access off; no backup software or backup drive set up besides the sync client

title: Legacy engineering virtual machine settings
source_system: Virtual machine settings on the service laptop (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: One virtual machine runs the legacy engineering package for older winding machine controllers; its operating system no longer receives updates from its maker and none has been installed in it; no malicious code protection inside it; its network adapter is set to bridged, so it joins whatever network the laptop is on

title: Phone settings and app review
source_system: Mobile phone settings screens (SYS-04)
what_it_shows: Passcode, device encryption and remote wipe on; automatic updates on; apps include the suite's email app, the authenticator app (the only MFA device), the vibration analytics app and a consumer generative AI assistant; the camera roll holds photos of nameplates, wiring and HMI screens and syncs to the owner's personal photo cloud; a personal hotspot is set up

title: Field connection kit inventory
source_system: Field connection kit in the service van (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: 8 USB sticks, none encrypted, holding program files for more than one customer; programming cables and adapters; a small unmanaged switch

title: Home office and service van walk-through
source_system: Home office and service van (observation)
what_it_shows: Florida home office with a locked file cabinet for paper records; the old laptop, replaced in 2025, is in a desk drawer and holds a copy of the Customer Machine Library, with no wipe or disposal record; the service van locks, has an alarm, and carries tools, test instruments and spare parts; the service laptop is kept in the home office overnight

title: Home router app: networks and connected devices
source_system: Internet provider's router app (SYS-09)
what_it_shows: One Wi-Fi network in use; a guest network is available and turned off; connected devices include the service laptop, family laptops, a smart TV and a game console

title: Router maker cloud portal: account and device settings
source_system: Router maker's cloud portal (SYS-06)
what_it_shows: The portal account is in the owner's name and signs in with a password only; MFA is offered and off; one cellular router is registered, on Customer B's vacuum drying oven control panel, online continuously since installation in 2024-11; remote sessions start with no approval step; the connection log is kept at the default retention setting

title: Router purchase record and Customer B request emails
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-01); accounting SaaS expense records (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: The owner bought the cellular router in 2024-11 after the Customer B maintenance supervisor asked by email for night and weekend remote support; no approval from Customer B's plant management appears in the inbox or the agreements folder

title: Customer A service agreement and Contractor Cyber Security Exhibit
source_system: Signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: Agreement renewed 2025-09-30 for two years, with confidentiality terms and exhibit S1 to S8: no disclosure of Customer A information to a third party, including cloud and AI services other than the contractor's own email and file storage, without written consent (S1); remote access only through Customer A's gateway and no contractor-installed remote access devices (S2); laptop and removable media scanned at the plant's station before connecting to plant equipment (S3); incident notice within 24 hours and coordination of the response (S4); hash verification before loading firmware or software (S5); utility access rules and notice within 1 business day when a person should no longer have utility site access (S6); return or secure deletion of information (S7); cyber liability insurance of at least $1 million from the 2027-09-30 renewal (S8)

title: Customer A letters of 2025-09-30
source_system: Signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: Customer A states that its substation work falls under the Supplier Cyber Security Addenda in its utility contracts, which follow NERC CIP-013-2 Requirement R1 Part 1.2, and that exhibit S4, S5 and S6 flow down those topics; inside substations the owner works escorted by utility staff with no unescorted physical or electronic access to utility systems; the service work involves no FAR or DFARS clauses, no federal contract information and no CUI

title: Customer NDAs and other customer terms on file
source_system: Signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: Mutual NDAs with Customers B and C: protect confidential information with reasonable care, use it only for the services, and give prompt written notice of any unauthorized disclosure, with no fixed number of days; no written security terms with the seven local plants

title: Customer A remote access gateway account
source_system: Customer A remote access gateway (SYS-07)
what_it_shows: Named account for the owner; MFA required at sign-in; each session is approved by the Customer A plant controls engineer; Customer A records the sessions

title: Customer A job tickets, 2025-08-20 to 2026-08-19
source_system: Job tickets in cloud file storage (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About 6 night breakdown calls at Customer A plants in the 12 months; the tickets have no field for media scanning and none records a visit to the scanning station

title: Substation firmware load records, 2026
source_system: Job tickets and firmware files for Customer A substation work (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Monitoring unit firmware was loaded on 4 substation cabinets in 2026; Customer A's hash values were received with the firmware files; no ticket records a hash check

title: Sent mail and inbox search: OEM support and customer consents
source_system: Email (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Program files and sharing links were emailed to OEM support desks in 2025 and 2026 for diagnosis; no request to a customer for consent, and no customer consent, appears for those messages or for the vibration analytics trial

title: Search of the owner's files for security documents
source_system: Laptop; cloud file storage; email; home office file cabinet
what_it_shows: No written security policy, risk assessment or risk tolerance, list of contract security duties, incident plan, incident criteria or contact list, customer notice procedure, contingency plan, emergency access sheet, referral arrangement with another technician, list of engineering software and licenses, or data return or disposal rule was found

title: Training and certification records
source_system: Owner's certificates folder (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: No security or awareness course certificate and no security newsletter or advisory subscription appears

title: General liability policy declarations
source_system: Insurance agent portal
what_it_shows: General liability coverage in force; no cyber coverage is listed

title: Insurance equipment schedule
source_system: Insurance agent portal
what_it_shows: Lists the laptop, the phone and the test instruments; the USB sticks, the router at Customer B and the old laptop are not listed

title: Bank and card statements, 2025-08-01 to 2026-07-31
source_system: Business bank account and card statements
what_it_shows: Recurring payments to the productivity suite provider (business plan), the accounting SaaS provider, the phone carrier, the internet provider and the general liability insurer; monthly payments to the CPA firm; hourly payments to the IT consultant; no payment for cyber insurance, a backup service, a password manager, or a security course

title: 2025 Schedule C (Form 1040)
source_system: Owner's tax files (prepared by the CPA firm)
what_it_shows: Gross receipts of about $180,000; no wages paid; the business is a sole proprietorship with no employees

title: Receipts by customer and job type, 2025-08-01 to 2026-07-31
source_system: Accounting SaaS reports (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: About 10 active business customers and no consumers; Customer A about 45% of receipts (about 35% plant service and about 10% substation field work), Customer B about 20%, Customer C about 15%, seven local plants about 20%; breakdown calls about 40% of receipts at premium rates; about $3,500 invoiced per week; customers pay by bank transfer or check, in 30 to 45 days

title: Customer purchase orders, 2025-08-01 to 2026-07-31
source_system: Email (SYS-01); accounting SaaS (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: The POs cover repair, maintenance and substation cabinet services; none carries a FAR or DFARS clause; every work site is in the United States; no PO involves a shipment abroad or a vehicle product

title: Vibration analytics trial account and dashboard
source_system: Vibration analytics SaaS and phone app (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: Trial account opened 2026-05-04; sensors on 6 motors at Customer A (winding line and drying oven vacuum pumps) and 4 motors at one local plant; uploaded data includes vibration and temperature readings, motor nameplate data, and machine and plant names

title: Vibration analytics trial terms, as accepted
source_system: Vibration analytics vendor website
what_it_shows: Click-through trial terms; the vendor may use uploaded data to improve its service

title: IT consultant NDA and invoices
source_system: Signed agreements folder; email (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: The consultant signed the owner's NDA on 2026-08-20; hourly invoices for help with the laptop, the virtual machine and the home router, given in remote-support sessions on the laptop

title: Bookkeeper engagement letter
source_system: Signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: The CPA firm does the monthly bookkeeping and the tax returns, working in the accounting SaaS through its own named login

title: Productivity suite provider SOC 2 Type 2 report
source_system: Productivity suite provider trust portal
what_it_shows: Type 2 report on the Security, Availability and Confidentiality categories for the 12 months ending 2026-06-30; unqualified opinion; one exception (2 of 40 sampled terminated provider employees kept access longer than the stated period), remediated; lists complementary user entity controls (MFA, user access and sharing permissions, device protection, the customer's own backups); data center hosting is a carved-out subservice organization

title: BIA self-review worksheet
source_system: Owner-technician's written BIA worksheet, reviewed with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: For each of the five business functions, the owner's account of the systems, vendors and customers involved, the manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss the function can tolerate; older machines at Customer B and two local plants load programs only from a USB stick; the owner has about two months of expenses in savings; the owner is the only person who performs each function

title: Risk walk-through of devices, accounts and the router at Customer B
source_system: Walk-through of the laptop, phone, field kit, SaaS accounts and the router at Customer B with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: How the laptop moves between email, web and customer machine networks; where customer programs and passwords are kept and carried; how USB sticks move between plants; how the router at Customer B is reached; how the 2026 firmware loads were made; what was uploaded to the AI trial

title: Gap analysis self-review
source_system: Owner-technician's written answers to the CSF 2.0 and contract term questions, checked on screen with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: Customer A's scanning station was skipped on about 6 night breakdown calls in the last 12 months; USB sticks and the laptop are not scanned before connecting at other plants; all Customer A remote work goes through its gateway and no owner device is installed at Customer A; the owner works alone and escorted at utility sites; engineering software is updated only when a job needs it; no subscription to CISA ICS advisories or makers' security notices; nobody reviews the SaaS sign-in history or the router portal log; after a reload only a machine test run confirms the program; the 4 firmware loads were made without a hash check

title: AI use self-review and vendor business plan terms
source_system: Owner-technician's AI use self-review; vibration analytics dashboard and vendor website
what_it_shows: Of the 3 trial alerts, 2 were confirmed with handheld readings (bearing wear on a vacuum pump motor; motor misalignment on the winding line) and 1 was a false positive after a sensor came loose; the vendor's paid business plan offers a data addendum that bars training on customer data and deletes data within 30 days of a request; the owner uses the consumer AI assistant to draft emails and quotes and to look up published fault code meanings, and states that no customer files were pasted into it

title: Customer B agreement on router use
source_system: Email from Customer B (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Customer B agrees that the router stays powered off except for sessions it approves by phone, until its plant management decides between a Customer B owned gateway and removal

title: Control assessment: Remote access test at Customer B
source_system: Router local admin page and portal session settings at Customer B; Customer A gateway account; owner self-review
what_it_shows: With Customer B's maintenance supervisor present: the router had no written usage restrictions or implementation guidance, a password-only cloud portal, and sessions with no per-session approval; its local admin page accepted the factory default password, which was changed during the test; no written authorization from Customer B plant management; Customer A's gateway has usage rules set by Customer A and Customer A approves each session

title: Control assessment: Administrator MFA sign-in test
source_system: Sign-ins from a new browser to the suite, the accounting SaaS and the router portal
what_it_shows: The suite administrator sign-in required the authenticator code; the accounting SaaS administrator account and the router portal account accepted a password only

title: Control assessment: Backup review and test restore
source_system: Suite retention settings; test restore of one machine folder (40 files) from version history
what_it_shows: The library and business records exist only on the laptop and its synced copy; no image of the laptop, the engineering software or the virtual machine; drawings, manuals and contract documents are only in the synced file plan; the provider encrypts stored files and the laptop is encrypted; no hash or record shows that a restored file is the unaltered current version; the 40-file folder restored from version history one file at a time

title: Control assessment: Malicious code protection test
source_system: Antivirus status page; standard antivirus test file downloaded on the laptop; virtual machine settings
what_it_shows: The built-in antivirus detected and quarantined the test file within seconds; signature updates are automatic, last update the same day; weekly quick scan scheduled and running; real-time scanning on for downloads and files opened from USB sticks; quarantine on detection; alert shown to the owner; no false positives on engineering software in the last 12 months and no exclusions set; the legacy virtual machine has no malicious code protection

title: Control assessment: Removable media review
source_system: Field kit (8 USB sticks); Customer A scanning station practice; owner self-review
what_it_shows: All 8 sticks are the owner's and the owner does not use sticks handed over by plant staff; the sticks are unencrypted, used for more than one customer and not scanned before plant use; the Customer A station was skipped on about 6 night calls in 12 months

title: Control assessment: Firmware and program integrity review
source_system: Firmware load records for 4 substation cabinets (2026); OS code-signing settings; library folder; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The operating system verifies code signatures on installed software and blocks unsigned or altered software, and the antivirus alerts the owner; engineering software comes from the makers' official sites; monitoring unit firmware was loaded on 4 cabinets without checking Customer A's hash values; no hash or version record for library programs; no defined action for a firmware hash mismatch or for a program that differs from the library copy

title: Control assessment: Boundary protection test
source_system: Home network walk-through; laptop firewall and virtual machine network settings; router at Customer B
what_it_shows: Tests on 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-27: laptop host firewall on for all network profiles and the provider router blocks inbound connections; no monitoring at the home internet connection or the router at Customer B; laptop-to-machine connections are not logged; the virtual machine reached the home network and the internet through its bridged adapter; Wi-Fi stayed on while the laptop was cabled to a machine network; the router at Customer B sat directly on the oven panel network; household devices share the home network with the laptop

title: Control assessment: Authenticator management review
source_system: SaaS password settings; cloud storage (password spreadsheet); router local admin page
what_it_shows: The owner set up each account directly with the provider; the bookkeeper's login was issued through the accounting SaaS invitation; SaaS passwords are unique, long and generated by the browser, whose password store is protected by the encrypted OS account; about 140 customer machine passwords sit in an unprotected spreadsheet; the router local admin page still had the factory default password (changed during the test); no procedure for lost or compromised authenticators or for revoking customer machine passwords; customer machine passwords are not changed when work for a customer ends; no written rule on protecting passwords; no group or role accounts

title: Control assessment: Incident reporting self-review
source_system: Contract file; owner self-review
what_it_shows: No time set for recording suspected incidents and no incident criteria; no contact list or procedure for the Customer A 24-hour notice or the NDA notices

title: Control assessment: Supplier review
source_system: Supplier terms; productivity suite SOC 2 report; vibration analytics trial terms
what_it_shows: No security requirements defined for suppliers and no documented oversight; the trial terms allow use of uploaded customer data and Customer A has not consented; the suite provider's SOC 2 Type 2 report, reviewed 2026-08-26, shows encryption, MFA support and backup controls; no ongoing monitoring of the other three SaaS suppliers; the bookkeeper has an accountant role and the IT consultant works only in owner-watched sessions under NDA
